Register an alias for a bank of sounds.
Optionally accepts a single argument map of bank aliases.
Optionally accepts a single argument string of a path to a JSON file containing bank aliases.

params.name: alias
params.description: The alias to use for the bank

allTransforms.name: allTransforms
allTransforms.description:
Applies a function to all the running patterns. Note that the patterns are groups together into a single stack before the function is applied. This is probably what you want, but see each for
a version that applies the function to each pattern separately.

$: sound("bd - cp sd")
$: sound("hh*8")
all(fast("<2 3>"))

$: sound("bd - cp sd")
$: sound("hh*8")
all(x => x.pianoroll())

anchor.name: anchor
anchor.description: The top note to align the voicing to. Defaults to c5

params.name: anchorNote
params.description: the note to align the voicings to

appBoth.name: appBoth
appBoth.description:
When this method is called on a pattern of functions, it matches its haps
with those in the given pattern of values.  A new pattern is returned, with
each matching value applied to the corresponding function.

In this _appBoth variant, where timespans of the function and value haps
are not the same but do intersect, the resulting hap has a timespan of the
intersection. This applies to both the part and the whole timespan.

appLeft.name: appLeft
appLeft.description:
As with appBoth, but the whole timespan is not the intersection,
but the timespan from the function of patterns that this method is called
on. In practice, this means that the pattern structure, including onsets,
are preserved from the pattern of functions (often referred to as the left
hand or inner pattern).

apply.name: apply
apply.description: Layers the result of the given function(s). Like superimpose, but without the original pattern:

applyGradualLowpass.name: applyGradualLowpass
applyGradualLowpass.description: Applies a constantly changing lowpass filter to the given sound.

params.name: callback
params.description:
May be called
immediately within the current execution context, or later.

appRight.name: appRight
appRight.description:
As with appLeft, but whole timespans are instead taken from the
pattern of values, i.e. structure is preserved from the right hand/outer
pattern.

appWhole.name: appWhole
appWhole.description:
Assumes 'this' is a pattern of functions, and given a function to
resolve wholes, applies a given pattern of values to that
pattern of functions.

arp.description: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

arpWith.description: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

Takes a variable number of arrays with two elements specifying the number of cycles and the pattern to use.

creates a structure pattern from divisions of a cycle
especially useful for creating rhythms

params.name: amount

berlin.name: berlin
berlin.description:
Generates a continuous pattern of [berlin noise](conceived by Jame Coyne and Jade Rowland as a joke but turned out to be surprisingly cool and useful,
like perlin noise but with sawtooth waves), in the range 0..1.

bite.name: bite
bite.description:
Splits a pattern into the given number of slices, and plays them according to a pattern of slice numbers.
Similar to slice, but slices up patterns rather than sound samples.

bmod.name: bmod
bmod.description:
Modulates with the output from a given bus.
Can be called in sequence like pat.bmod(...).bmod(...) to set up multiple modulators

Send to an audio bus with otherPat.bus(..).

There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:


Explicitly put control in the config (e.g. bmod({ id: 2, c: "lpf" }))

If the control parameter is absent, the control immediately before the bmod call will be used
(e.g. s("saw").lpf(500).bmod({ id: 2 }) to modulate lpf)


Modulators can be referred to by id so that they can be updated later e.g. inside
a sometimes. See example below.

params.description: Bus to get modulation signal from

params.description: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc

params.name: config.depth
params.description: Relative modulation depth. Aliases: dep, dr

params.name: id
params.description: ID to use for this modulator

brak.name: brak
brak.description:
Returns a new pattern where every other cycle is played once, twice as
fast, and offset in time by one quarter of a cycle. Creates a kind of
breakbeat feel.

brand.name: brand
brand.description: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random)

brandBy.name: brandBy
brandBy.description: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random), with a probability for the value being 1

bus.name: bus
bus.description:
A bus is a send which can be used for mixing patterns. It combines with..
s("bus") to play that bus through another pattern (for, say, applying non-linear
effects like distortion to multiple signals)

otherPat.bmod(..) (to modulate another pattern with the bus)

busgain.name: busgain
busgain.description: Postgain multiplier prior to sending the signal to the audio bus.

byteBeatExpression.name: byteBeatExpression
byteBeatExpression.description: Create byte beats with custom expressions

byteBeatStartTime.name: byteBeatStartTime
byteBeatStartTime.description: Create byte beats with custom expressions

cat.name: cat
cat.description: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle.

ccn.name: ccn
ccn.description: MIDI control number: Sends a MIDI control change message.

ccv.name: ccv
ccv.description: MIDI control value: Sends a MIDI control change message.

ceil.name: ceil
ceil.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to
their mathematical ceiling. E.g. 3.2 replaced with 4, and -4.2
replaced with -4.

ch.name: ch
ch.description: Allows you to set the output channels on the interface

channel.name: channel
channel.description: Choose the channel the pattern is sent to in superdirt

channels.name: channels
channels.description: Allows you to set the output channels on the interface

choose.name: choose
choose.description:
Chooses from the given list of values (or patterns of values), according
to the pattern that the method is called on. The pattern should be in
the range 0 .. 1.

choose2.name: choose2
choose2.description:
As with choose, but the pattern that this method is called on should be
in the range -1 .. 1

chooseCycles.name: chooseCycles
chooseCycles.description: Picks one of the elements at random each cycle.

chooseInWith.name: chooseInWith
chooseInWith.description:
As with {chooseWith}, but the structure comes from the chosen values, rather
than the pattern you're using to choose with.

chooseWith.name: chooseWith
chooseWith.description:
Choose from the list of values (or patterns of values) using the given
pattern of numbers, which should be in the range of 0..1

chop.name: chop
chop.description:
Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, allowing you to explore a technique known as 'granular synthesis'.
It turns a pattern of samples into a pattern of parts of samples.
examples:
samples({ rhodes: 'https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/132/132051_316502-lq.mp3' })
s("rhodes")
 .chop(4)
 .rev() // reverse order of chops
 .loopAt(2) // fit sample into 2 cycles

chord.name: chord

params.name: symbols
params.description: chord symbols to voice e.g., C, Eb, Fm7, G7. The symbols can be defined via addVoicings

examples: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").voicing()

chorus.name: chorus
chorus.description: mix control for the chorus effect

chunk.name: chunk
chunk.description: Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

chunkback.name: chunkback
chunkback.description: Like chunk, but cycles through the parts in reverse order. Known as chunk' in tidalcycles

chunkBack.name: chunkBack
chunkBack.description: Like chunk, but cycles through the parts in reverse order. Known as chunk' in tidalcycles

chunkbackinto.name: chunkbackinto
chunkbackinto.description: Like chunkInto, but moves backwards through the chunks.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

chunkBackInto.name: chunkBackInto
chunkBackInto.description: Like chunkInto, but moves backwards through the chunks.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

chunkinto.name: chunkinto
chunkinto.description: Like chunk, but the function is applied to a looped subcycle of the source pattern.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

chunkInto.name: chunkInto
chunkInto.description: Like chunk, but the function is applied to a looped subcycle of the source pattern.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

clip.name: clip
clip.description: Multiplies the duration with the given number. Also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

coarse.name: coarse
coarse.description: Fake-resampling for lowering the sample rate. Caution: This effect seems to only work in chromium based browsers

params.name: factor
params.description: 1 for original 2 for half, 3 for a third and so on.

color.name: color
color.description: Sets the color of the hap in visualizations like pianoroll or highlighting.

colour.name: colour
colour.description: Sets the color of the hap in visualizations like pianoroll or highlighting.

compress.name: compress
compress.description: Compress each cycle into the given timespan, leaving a gap
examples:
cat(
  s("bd sd").compress(.25,.75),
  s("~ bd sd ~")
)

compressor.name: compressor
compressor.description:
Dynamics Compressor. The params are compressor("threshold:ratio:knee:attack:release")
More info here

computeMagnitudes.name: computeMagnitudes
computeMagnitudes.description: Compute squared magnitudes for peak finding

contract.name: contract
contract.description:
Experimental

Contracts the step size of the pattern by the given factor. See also expand.

control.name: control
control.description: MIDI control: Sends a MIDI control change message.

cosine2.name: cosine2
cosine2.description: A cosine signal between -1 and 1 (like cosine, but bipolar).

cpm.name: cpm
cpm.description: Plays the pattern at the given cycles per minute.

crossfade.name: crossfade
crossfade.description:
Equal Power Crossfade function.
Smoothly transitions between signals A and B, maintaining consistent perceived loudness.

params.name: a
params.description: Signal A (can be a single value or an array value in buffer processing).

params.name: b
params.description: Signal B (can be a single value or an array value in buffer processing).

params.name: m
params.description: Crossfade parameter (0.0 = all A, 1.0 = all B, 0.5 = equal mix).

params.name: depth
params.description: between 1 (for drastic reduction in bit-depth) to 16 (for barely no reduction).

csoundm.name: csoundm
csoundm.description:
Sends notes to Csound for rendering with MIDI semantics. The hap value is
translated to these Csound pfields:

p1 -- Csound instrument either as a number (1-based, can be a fraction),
or as a string name.
p2 -- time in beats (usually seconds) from start of performance.
p3 -- duration in beats (usually seconds).
p4 -- MIDI key number (as a real number, not an integer but in [0, 127].
p5 -- MIDI velocity (as a real number, not an integer but in [0, 127].
p6 -- Strudel controls, as a string.

ctf.name: ctf
ctf.description:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the low-pass filter.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'lpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

cut.name: cut
cut.description: In the style of classic drum-machines, cut will stop a playing sample as soon as another samples with in same cutgroup is to be played. An example would be an open hi-hat followed by a closed one, essentially muting the open.

cutoff.name: cutoff
cutoff.description:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the low-pass filter.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'lpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

cyclesPer.name: cyclesPer
cyclesPer.description:
A pattern measuring the duration of events,
in cycles per event. cyclesPer doesn't have structure itself, but takes structure, and therefore
event durations, from the pattern that it is combined with.
For example cyclesPer.struct("1 1 [1 1] 1") would give the same as "0.25 0.25 [0.125 0.125] 0.25".
See also its reciprocal, per, also known as perCycle.
examples:
sound("bd sd [bd bd] sd*4 [- sd] [bd [bd bd]]")
  .note(cyclesPer.add(20))

dec.name: dec
dec.description:
Amplitude envelope decay time: the time it takes after the attack time to reach the sustain level.
Note that the decay is only audible if the sustain value is lower than 1.

decay.name: decay
decay.description:
Amplitude envelope decay time: the time it takes after the attack time to reach the sustain level.
Note that the decay is only audible if the sustain value is lower than 1.

defaultmidimap.name: defaultmidimap
defaultmidimap.description: configures the default midimap, which is used when no "midimap" port is set

defragmentHaps.name: defragmentHaps
defragmentHaps.description:
Combines adjacent haps with the same value and whole.  Only
intended for use in tests.

degrade.name: degrade
degrade.description: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for .degradeBy(0.5)

degradeBy.name: degradeBy
degradeBy.description:
Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount.
0 = 0% chance of removal
1 = 100% chance of removal

delay.name: delay
delay.description:
Sets the level of the delay signal.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'delaytime' and 'delayfeedback' parameter,
separated by ':'.

delayfb.name: delayfb
delayfb.description:
Sets the level of the signal that is fed back into the delay.
Caution: Values >= 1 will result in a signal that gets louder and louder! Don't do it

delayfeedback.name: delayfeedback
delayfeedback.description:
Sets the level of the signal that is fed back into the delay.
Caution: Values >= 1 will result in a signal that gets louder and louder! Don't do it

delayspeed.name: delayspeed
delayspeed.description: Sets the time of the delay effect.

params.name: delayspeed
params.description: controls the pitch of the delay feedback

delaysync.name: delaysync
delaysync.description: Sets the time of the delay effect in cycles.

delayt.name: delayt
delayt.description: Sets the time of the delay effect in cycles.

density.name: density
density.description: Speed up a pattern by the given factor. Used by "*" in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").fast(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]*2")

det.name: det
det.description: Set detune for stacked voices of supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").detune("<.1 .2 .5 24.1>")

detune.name: detune
detune.description: Set detune for stacked voices of supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").detune("<.1 .2 .5 24.1>")

dfb.name: dfb
dfb.description:
Sets the level of the signal that is fed back into the delay.
Caution: Values >= 1 will result in a signal that gets louder and louder! Don't do it

dictionary.name: dictionary
dictionary.description: Which dictionary to use for the voicings. This falls back to the default dictionary if not provided

params.name: dictionaryName
params.description: which dictionary (having been defined with addVoicings) to use

examples:
addVoicings('house', {
'': ['7 12 16', '0 7 16', '4 7 12'],
'm': ['0 3 7']
})
chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>")
.dict('house').anchor(66)
.voicing().room(.5)

discreteOnly.name: discreteOnly
discreteOnly.description:
Returns a new pattern, with 'continuous' haps (those without 'whole'
timespans) removed from query results.

dist.name: dist
dist.description:
Wave shaping distortion. CAUTION: it can get loud.
Second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output. Third option sets the waveshaping type.
Most useful values are usually between 0 and 10 (depending on source gain). If you are feeling adventurous, you can turn it up to 11 and beyond ;)

distort.name: distort
distort.description:
Wave shaping distortion. CAUTION: it can get loud.
Second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output. Third option sets the waveshaping type.
Most useful values are usually between 0 and 10 (depending on source gain). If you are feeling adventurous, you can turn it up to 11 and beyond ;)

distorttype.name: distorttype
distorttype.description: Type of waveshaping distortion to apply.
examples:
s("sine").note("F1*2").release(1)
  .penv(24).pdecay(0.05)
  .distort(rand.range(1, 8))
  .distorttype("<fold chebyshev scurve diode asym sinefold>")

disttype.name: disttype
disttype.description: Type of waveshaping distortion to apply.
examples:
s("sine").note("F1*2").release(1)
  .penv(24).pdecay(0.05)
  .distort(rand.range(1, 8))
  .distorttype("<fold chebyshev scurve diode asym sinefold>")

div.name: div
div.description: Divides each number by the given factor.

djf.name: djf
djf.description: DJ filter, below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter.

params.name: cutoff
params.description: below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter

drawFrequencyScope.name: drawFrequencyScope
signature: { color = 'white', scale = 0.25, pos = 0.75, lean = 0.5, min = -150, max = 0, ctx = getDrawContext(), id = 1 } = {}

drawLine.name: drawLine
drawLine.description:
Intended for a debugging, drawLine renders the pattern as a string, where each character represents the same time span.
Should only be used with single characters as values, otherwise the character slots will be messed up.
Character legend:


"|" cycle separator

"-" hold previous value

"." silence

drawSpectrum.name: drawSpectrum
signature: { thickness = 3, speed = 1, min = -80, max = 0, ctx = getDrawContext(), id = 1, color } = {}

drawTimeScope.name: drawTimeScope

drive.name: drive
drive.description: Filter overdrive for supported filter types
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%16".sub(17)).s("supersaw").lpenv(8).lpf(150).lpq(.8).ftype('ladder').drive("<.5 4>")

drop.name: drop
drop.description:
Experimental

Drops the given number of steps from a pattern.
A positive number will drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

dry.name: dry
dry.description: Set dryness of reverb. See room and size for more information about reverb.

dt.name: dt
dt.description: Sets the time of the delay effect in cycles.

duck.name: duck
duck.description:
Modulate the amplitude of an orbit to create a "sidechain" like effect.

Can be applied to multiple orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckorbit("2:3")

duckatt.name: duckatt
duckatt.description:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to return to their normal volume.

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003").
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").

duckattack.name: duckattack
duckattack.description:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to return to their normal volume.

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003").
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").

duckdepth.name: duckdepth
duckdepth.description:
The amount of ducking applied to target orbit

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckdepth("0.3:0.1").
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").

duckons.name: duckons
duckons.description:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to reach their lowest volume.
Can be used to prevent clicking or for creative rhythmic effects.

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003").
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").
examples:
// Rhythmic
noise: s("pink").distort("2:1").orbit(4) // used rhythmically with 0.3 onset below
hhat: s("hh*16").orbit(7)
ducker: s("bd*4").bank("tr909").duckorbit("4:7").duckonset("0.3:0.003").duckattack(0.25)

duckonset.name: duckonset
duckonset.description:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to reach their lowest volume.
Can be used to prevent clicking or for creative rhythmic effects.

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003").
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").
examples:
// Rhythmic
noise: s("pink").distort("2:1").orbit(4) // used rhythmically with 0.3 onset below
hhat: s("hh*16").orbit(7)
ducker: s("bd*4").bank("tr909").duckorbit("4:7").duckonset("0.3:0.003").duckattack(0.25)

duckorbit.name: duckorbit
duckorbit.description:
Modulate the amplitude of an orbit to create a "sidechain" like effect.

Can be applied to multiple orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckorbit("2:3")

dur.name: dur
dur.description: Sets the duration of the event in cycles. Similar to clip / legato, it also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

duration.name: duration
duration.description: Sets the duration of the event in cycles. Similar to clip / legato, it also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

each.name: each
each.description:
Applies a function to each of the running patterns separately. This is intended for future use with upcoming 'stepwise' features. See all for a version that applies the function to all the patterns stacked together into a single pattern.

$: sound("bd - cp sd")
$: sound("hh*8")
each(fast("<2 3>"))

early.name: early
early.description: Nudge a pattern to start earlier in time. Equivalent of Tidal's <~ operator

params.name: cycles
params.description: number of cycles to nudge left

echo.name: echo
echo.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, gradually decreasing the velocity

echowith.name: echowith
echowith.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

params.name: func
params.description: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

echoWith.name: echoWith
echoWith.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

params.name: func
params.description: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

eish.name: eish
eish.description:
A 'euclid' variant with an additional parameter that morphs the resulting
rhythm from 0 (no morphing) to 1 (completely 'even'). For example
sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0) would be the same as
sound("bd").euclid(3,8), and sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,1) would be the
same as sound("bd bd bd"). sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0.5) would have a
groove somewhere between.
Inspired by the work of Malcom Braff.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

params.name: groove
params.description: exists between the extremes of 0 (straight euclidian) and 1 (straight pulse)

end.name: end
end.description: The same as .begin, but cuts off the end off each sample.

params.name: length
params.description: 1 = whole sample, .5 = half sample, .25 = quarter sample etc..

env.name: env
env.description:
Configures an envelope. Can be called in sequence like pat.env(...).env(...) to set up multiple envelopes
There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:


Explicitly put control in the config (e.g. env({ c: "lpf" }))

If the control parameter is absent, the control immediately before the env call will be used
(e.g. s("saw").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 }) to modulate lpf)


Modulators can be referred to by id so that they can be updated later e.g. inside
a sometimes. See example below.

params.name: config.subControl
params.description: Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc

params.name: config.depth
params.description: Relative modulation depth. Aliases: dep, dr

params.name: config.attack
params.description: Time to reach depth. Aliases: att, a

params.name: config.decay
params.description: Time to reach sustain. Aliases: dec, d

params.name: config.release
params.description: Time to return to nominal value. Aliases: rel, r

params.name: config.acurve
params.description: Snappiness of attack curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: ac

params.name: config.dcurve
params.description: Snappiness of decay curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: dc

params.name: config.rcurve
params.description: Snappiness of release curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: rc

params.name: id
params.description: ID to use for this modulator

examples:
s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 })
  .env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 1)) // envelope #1 (0-indexed)

s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 }, 'lpf_mod')
  .env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
  .diode(0.3)
  .sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 'lpf_mod'))

euclid.name: euclid
euclid.description:
Changes the structure of the pattern to form an Euclidean rhythm.
Euclidean rhythms are rhythms obtained using the greatest common
divisor of two numbers.  They were described in 2004 by Godfried
Toussaint, a Canadian computer scientist.  Euclidean rhythms are
really useful for computer/algorithmic music because they can
describe a large number of rhythms with a couple of numbers.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

euclidish.name: euclidish
euclidish.description:
A 'euclid' variant with an additional parameter that morphs the resulting
rhythm from 0 (no morphing) to 1 (completely 'even'). For example
sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0) would be the same as
sound("bd").euclid(3,8), and sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,1) would be the
same as sound("bd bd bd"). sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0.5) would have a
groove somewhere between.
Inspired by the work of Malcom Braff.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

params.name: groove
params.description: exists between the extremes of 0 (straight euclidian) and 1 (straight pulse)

euclidLegato.name: euclidLegato
euclidLegato.description:
Similar to euclid, but each pulse is held until the next pulse,
so there will be no gaps.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

euclidLegatoRot.name: euclidLegatoRot
euclidLegatoRot.description:
Similar to euclid, but each pulse is held until the next pulse,
so there will be no gaps, and has an additional parameter for 'rotating'
the resulting sequence

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

euclidRot.name: euclidRot
euclidRot.description: Like euclid, but has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

examples:
// A Samba rhythm necklace from Brazil
note("c3").euclidRot(3,16,14)

expand.name: expand
expand.description:
Experimental

Expands the step size of the pattern by the given factor.

extend.name: extend
extend.description:
Experimental

extend is similar to fast in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count
accordingly. So stepcat("a b".extend(2), "c d") would be the same as "a b a b c d", whereas
stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d") would be the same as "[a b] [a b] c d".
examples:
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - cp").extend(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)

fanchor.name: fanchor
fanchor.description: controls the center of the filter envelope. 0 is unipolar positive, .5 is bipolar, 1 is unipolar negative
examples:
note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpf("{1000}%2")
.lpenv(8).fanchor("<0 .5 1>")

fast.name: fast
fast.description: Speed up a pattern by the given factor. Used by "*" in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").fast(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]*2")

fastcat.name: fastcat
fastcat.description: Like cat, but the items are crammed into one cycle.

fastchunk.name: fastchunk
fastchunk.description:
Like chunk, but the cycles of the source pattern aren't repeated
for each set of chunks.

fastChunk.name: fastChunk
fastChunk.description:
Like chunk, but the cycles of the source pattern aren't repeated
for each set of chunks.

fastgap.name: fastgap
fastgap.description: speeds up a pattern like fast, but rather than it playing multiple times as fast would it instead leaves a gap in the remaining space of the cycle. For example, the following will play the sound pattern "bd sn" only once but compressed into the first half of the cycle, i.e. twice as fast.

fastGap.name: fastGap
fastGap.description: speeds up a pattern like fast, but rather than it playing multiple times as fast would it instead leaves a gap in the remaining space of the cycle. For example, the following will play the sound pattern "bd sn" only once but compressed into the first half of the cycle, i.e. twice as fast.

filter.name: filter
filter.description: Filters haps using the given function

filterHaps.name: filterHaps
filterHaps.description: Returns a new Pattern, which only returns haps that meet the given test.

params.name: hap_test
params.description: a function which returns false for haps to be removed from the pattern

filterValues.name: filterValues
filterValues.description:
As with filterHaps, but the function is applied to values
inside haps.
examples:
const drums = s("bd sd bd sd")
kick: drums.filterValues((v) => v.s === 'bd').duck(2)
snare: drums.filterValues((v) => v.s === 'sd')
bass: s("saw!4").note("G#1").lpf(80).lpenv(4).orbit(2)

filterWhen.name: filterWhen
filterWhen.description: Filters haps by their begin time

firstCycle.name: firstCycle
firstCycle.description:
Queries the pattern for the first cycle, returning Haps. Mainly of use when
debugging a pattern.

params.name: with_context
params.description:
set to true, otherwise the context field
will be stripped from the resulting haps.

firstCycleValues.name: firstCycleValues
firstCycleValues.description: Accessor for a list of values returned by querying the first cycle.

firstOf.name: firstOf
firstOf.description: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the first cycle.

fit.name: fit
fit.description:
Makes the sample fit its event duration. Good for rhythmical loops like drum breaks.
Similar to loopAt.

floor.name: floor
floor.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to
their mathematical floor. E.g. 3.7 replaced with to 3, and -4.2
replaced with -5.

fm.name: fm
fm.description:
Sets the Frequency Modulation of the synth.
Controls the modulation index, which defines the brightness of the sound.

A number may be added afterwards to control the modulation index of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fm3). Also, FMs may be routed into
each other with matrix commands like fm13, which would send fm1 back into
fm3
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm("<0 1 2 8 32>")
._scope()

fmap.name: fmap
fmap.description:
Returns a new pattern, with the function applied to the value of
each hap. It has the alias fmap.

params.name: func
params.description: to to apply to the value

fmatt.name: fmatt
fmatt.description:
Attack time for the FM envelope: time it takes to reach maximum modulation

A number may be added afterwards to control the attack of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmatt5)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmattack("<0 .05 .1 .2>")
._scope()

fmattack.name: fmattack
fmattack.description:
Attack time for the FM envelope: time it takes to reach maximum modulation

A number may be added afterwards to control the attack of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmatt5)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmattack("<0 .05 .1 .2>")
._scope()

fmdec.name: fmdec
fmdec.description:
Decay time for the FM envelope: seconds until the sustain level is reached after the attack phase.

A number may be added afterwards to control the decay of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmdec6)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay("<.01 .05 .1 .2>")
.fmsustain(.4)
._scope()

fmdecay.name: fmdecay
fmdecay.description:
Decay time for the FM envelope: seconds until the sustain level is reached after the attack phase.

A number may be added afterwards to control the decay of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmdec6)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay("<.01 .05 .1 .2>")
.fmsustain(.4)
._scope()

fmenv.name: fmenv
fmenv.description:
Ramp type of fm envelope. Exp might be a bit broken..

A number may be added afterwards to control the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmenv4)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.2)
.fmsustain(0)
.fmenv("<exp lin>")
._scope()

fmh.name: fmh
fmh.description:
Sets the Frequency Modulation Harmonicity Ratio.
Controls the timbre of the sound.
Whole numbers and simple ratios sound more natural,
while decimal numbers and complex ratios sound metallic.

A number may be added afterwards to control the harmonicity of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmh2)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmh("<1 2 1.5 1.61>")
._scope()

fmi.name: fmi
fmi.description:
Sets the Frequency Modulation of the synth.
Controls the modulation index, which defines the brightness of the sound.

A number may be added afterwards to control the modulation index of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fm3). Also, FMs may be routed into
each other with matrix commands like fm13, which would send fm1 back into
fm3
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm("<0 1 2 8 32>")
._scope()

fmrel.name: fmrel
fmrel.description:
Release time for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the note is released

A number may be added afterwards to control the release of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmrel8)

fmrelease.name: fmrelease
fmrelease.description:
Release time for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the note is released

A number may be added afterwards to control the release of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmrel8)

fmsus.name: fmsus
fmsus.description:
Sustain level for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the decay phase

A number may be added afterwards to control the sustain of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmsus7)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.1)
.fmsustain("<1 .75 .5 0>")
._scope()

fmsustain.name: fmsustain
fmsustain.description:
Sustain level for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the decay phase

A number may be added afterwards to control the sustain of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmsus7)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.1)
.fmsustain("<1 .75 .5 0>")
._scope()

fmwave.name: fmwave
fmwave.description:
Waveform of the fm modulator

A number may be added afterwards to control the waveform
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. fmwave6)

focus.name: focus
focus.description: Similar to compress, but doesn't leave gaps, and the 'focus' can be bigger than a cycle

params.name: frequency
params.description: in Hz. the audible range is between 20 and 20000 Hz

fromBipolar.name: fromBipolar
fromBipolar.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the unipolar range 0 .. 1

fscope.name: fscope
fscope.description: Renders an oscilloscope for the frequency domain of the audio signal.

params.name: lean
params.description: y-axis alignment where 0 = top and 1 = bottom

ftype.name: ftype
ftype.description: Sets the filter type. The ladder filter is more aggressive. More types might be added in the future.
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpenv(4).lpf(500).ftype("<0 1 2>").lpq(1)

note("c f g g a c d4").fast(2)
.sound('sawtooth')
.lpf(200).fanchor(0)
.lpenv(3).lpq(1)
.ftype("<ladder 12db 24db>")

FX.name: FX
FX.description:
Establishes an FX chain. Can be called by chaining .FX(fx1).FX(fx2)..
calls and/or in a single .FX(fx1, fx2, ..) call. The fx1, .. are patterns which
establish the controls of the given effect. See examples.
examples:
$: s("[sbd <hh [bd | lt | oh]>]*4").dec(.4)
  .FX(
    phaser(0.5).gain(2),
    bpf(800),
    distort(1.3),
    room(0.2),
    delay(0.5).gain(1.25),
    distort(0.3),
  ).fxr(1.7) // sets release time of effects (like delay)

$: s("saw").fm(0.5)
  .delay(0.3) // outer effects are applied *last*
  .FX(coarse(4)) // first coarse
  .FX(lpf(500).lpe(4).lpa(1).lpd(2)) // then lpf
  .FX(distort(1)) // then distort

gain.name: gain
gain.description: Controls the gain by an exponential amount.

gap.name: gap
gap.description: Does absolutely nothing, but with a given metrical 'steps'

generateGraph.name: generateGraph
generateGraph.description: Creates a canvas element showing a graph of the given data.

gravY.name: gravY
gravY.description: The device's gravity y-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

gravZ.name: gravZ
gravZ.description: The device's gravity z-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

grow.name: grow
grow.description:
Experimental

Progressively grows the pattern by 'n' steps until the full pattern is played, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with :),
that number of times.
A positive number will progressively grow steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

handleOutputBuffersToRetrieve.name: handleOutputBuffersToRetrieve
handleOutputBuffersToRetrieve.description: Add contents of output buffers just processed to output buffers

hcutoff.name: hcutoff
hcutoff.description:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the high-pass filter.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'hpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

hp.name: hp
hp.description:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the high-pass filter.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'hpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

hpa.name: hpa
hpa.description: Sets the attack duration for the highpass filter envelope.

params.description: time of the highpass filter envelope

hpattack.name: hpattack
hpattack.description: Sets the attack duration for the highpass filter envelope.

params.name: attack
params.description: time of the highpass filter envelope

hpd.name: hpd
hpd.description: Sets the decay duration for the highpass filter envelope.

params.name: decay
params.description: time of the highpass filter envelope

hpdc.name: hpdc
hpdc.description: DC offset of the LFO for the highpass filter

params.description: dc offset. set to 0 for unipolar

hpdecay.name: hpdecay
hpdecay.description: Sets the decay duration for the highpass filter envelope.

params.name: decay
params.description: time of the highpass filter envelope

hpdepth.name: hpdepth
hpdepth.description: Depth of the LFO for the highpass filter

hpdepthfreq.name: hpdepthfreq
hpdepthfreq.description: Depth of the LFO for the hipass filter, in hz

hpdepthfrequency.name: hpdepthfrequency
hpdepthfrequency.description: Depth of the LFO for the hipass filter, in hz

hpe.name: hpe
hpe.description: Sets the highpass filter envelope modulation depth.

params.name: modulation
params.description: depth of the highpass filter envelope between 0 and n

hpenv.name: hpenv
hpenv.description: Sets the highpass filter envelope modulation depth.

params.name: modulation
params.description: depth of the highpass filter envelope between 0 and n

hpf.name: hpf
hpf.description:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the high-pass filter.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'hpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

hpr.name: hpr
hpr.description: Sets the release time for the highpass filter envelope.

params.name: release
params.description: time of the highpass filter envelope

hprate.name: hprate
hprate.description: Rate of the LFO for the highpass filter

hprelease.name: hprelease
hprelease.description: Sets the release time for the highpass filter envelope.

params.description: time of the highpass filter envelope

hps.name: hps
hps.description: Sets the sustain amplitude for the highpass filter envelope.

params.description: amplitude of the highpass filter envelope

hpshape.name: hpshape
hpshape.description: Shape of the LFO for the highpass filter

hpskew.name: hpskew
hpskew.description: Skew of the LFO for the highpass filter

params.name: skew
params.description: How much to bend the LFO shape

hpsustain.name: hpsustain
hpsustain.description: Sets the sustain amplitude for the highpass filter envelope.

params.name: sustain
params.description: amplitude of the highpass filter envelope

hpsync.name: hpsync
hpsync.description: Cycle-synced rate of the LFO for the highpass filter

hurry.name: hurry
hurry.description: Both speeds up the pattern (like 'fast') and the sample playback (like 'speed').

inhabit.name: inhabit
inhabit.description:
Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name).
Similar to pick, but cycles are squeezed into the target ('inhabited') pattern.

inhabitmod.name: inhabitmod
inhabitmod.description:
The same as inhabit, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.
For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the
second one.

inside.name: inside
inside.description: Carries out an operation 'inside' a cycle.

into.name: into
into.description:
Breaks a pattern into pieces according to the structure of a given pattern.
True values in the given pattern cause the corresponding subcycle of the
source pattern to be looped, and for an (optional) given function to be
applied. False values result in the corresponding part of the source pattern
to be played unchanged.

inv.name: inv
inv.description: Swaps 1s and 0s in a binary pattern.

invert.name: invert
invert.description: Swaps 1s and 0s in a binary pattern.

ir.name: ir
ir.description: Sets the beginning of the IR response sample

irand.name: irand
irand.description: A continuous pattern of random integers, between 0 and n-1.
examples:
// randomly select scale notes from 0 - 7 (= C to C)
n(irand(8)).struct("x x*2 x x*3").scale("C:minor")

irbegin.name: irbegin
irbegin.description: Sets the beginning of the IR response sample

iresponse.name: iresponse
iresponse.description: Sets the sample to use as an impulse response for the reverb.

params.name: sample
params.description: to use as an impulse response

irspeed.name: irspeed
irspeed.description: Sets speed of the sample for the impulse response.

isaw.name: isaw
isaw.description: A sawtooth signal between 1 and 0 (like saw, but flipped).

isaw2.name: isaw2
isaw2.description: A sawtooth signal between 1 and -1 (like saw2, but flipped).

iter.name: iter
iter.description: Divides a pattern into a given number of subdivisions, plays the subdivisions in order, but increments the starting subdivision each cycle. The pattern wraps to the first subdivision after the last subdivision is played.

iterback.name: iterback
iterback.description: Like iter, but plays the subdivisions in reverse order. Known as iter' in tidalcycles

iterBack.name: iterBack
iterBack.description: Like iter, but plays the subdivisions in reverse order. Known as iter' in tidalcycles

itri.name: itri
itri.description: An inverted triangle signal between 1 and 0 (like tri, but flipped).

itri2.name: itri2
itri2.description: An inverted triangle signal between -1 and 1 (like itri, but bipolar).

jux.name: jux
jux.description: The jux function creates strange stereo effects, by applying a function to a pattern, but only in the right-hand channel.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(rev)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(press)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(iter(4))

juxby.name: juxby
juxby.description: Jux with adjustable stereo width. 0 = mono, 1 = full stereo.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxBy("<0 .5 1>/2", rev)

juxBy.name: juxBy
juxBy.description: Jux with adjustable stereo width. 0 = mono, 1 = full stereo.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxBy("<0 .5 1>/2", rev)

K.name: K
K.description:
Produces a Kabelsalat modular sound engine.
This can be used as either an effect (by including audioin() at the beginning
of your kabel expression) or as a sound source (via any expression which doesn't
start with audioin()).

Some helpers you have available to you:


Strudel mini notation works fine in K(..) via "" or ``

More complex Strudel expressions (like "0 1 2".fast(4) or irand(24)) can be
written by wrapping them in S(..) inside your Kabel code

We expose Strudel's note frequency under sFreq and Strudel's gate
information under sGate

You can use more complex multi-line expressions (like let x = a; let y = b; x.lpf(y);)
by wrapping them inside a function in K (see example).
examples:
note("A c e".fast(4)).transpose("<0 2 4 6 8>")
  .scale("F:minor").transpose("12")
  .s("saw")
  .K(
    // audioin().mul(sGate.adsr(0.001, 0.3, 0, 0.2)) // as effect
    saw(saw(sFreq / "2!3 16").mul(8).add(sFreq).lag("0!3 0.1")).mul(0.3) // as source
    .mul(sGate.adsr(0, 0.15, 0.5, "0.1!3 1"))
    .lpf(sGate.adsr(0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.2).mul(1).add(0))
    .add(x => x.delay(S("0.3 0.2".fast(2))).mul(0.7))
    .add(x => x.delay("0.03 [0.08 0.01] 0.01 0.013").mul(0.77)).mul(0.7)
    .add(x => x.delay(.13).mul(0.7))
    .out()
  )

polymeter("c eb g", "c2 g2").note()

prepareInputBuffersToSend.description: Copy contents of input buffers to buffer actually sent to process

press.name: press
press.description: Syncopates a rhythm, by shifting each event halfway into its timespan.

pressBy.name: pressBy
pressBy.description:
Like press, but allows you to specify the amount by which each
event is shifted. pressBy(0.5) is the same as press, while
pressBy(1/3) shifts each event by a third of its timespan.

progNum.name: progNum
progNum.description: MIDI program number: Sends a MIDI program change message.

punchcard.name: punchcard
punchcard.description:
Visualises a pattern as a scrolling 'pianoroll', displayed in the background of the editor. To show a pianoroll for all running patterns, use all(pianoroll). To have a pianoroll appear below
a pattern instead, prefix with _, e.g.: sound("bd sd")._pianoroll().

params.name: options
params.description: Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:

params.name: cycles
params.description: number of cycles to be displayed at the same time - defaults to 4

params.name: playhead
params.description: location of the active notes on the time axis - 0 to 1, defaults to 0.5

params.name: vertical
params.description: displays the roll vertically - 0 by default

params.name: labels
params.description: displays labels on individual notes (see the label function) - 0 by default

params.name: flipTime
params.description: reverse the direction of the roll - 0 by default

params.name: flipValues
params.description: reverse the relative location of notes on the value axis - 0 by default

params.name: overscan
params.description: lookup X cycles outside of the cycles window to display notes in advance - 1 by default

params.name: hideNegative
params.description: hide notes with negative time (before starting playing the pattern) - 0 by default

params.name: smear
params.description: notes leave a solid trace - 0 by default

params.name: fold
params.description: notes takes the full value axis width - 0 by default

params.name: active
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the active notes - defaults to #FFCA28

params.name: inactive
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the inactive notes - defaults to #7491D2

params.name: background

params.name: playheadColor

params.name: fill

params.name: fillActive

params.name: stroke

params.name: hideInactive

params.name: colorizeInactive

params.name: fontFamily
params.description: define the font used by notes labels - defaults to 'monospace'

params.name: minMidi

params.name: maxMidi

params.name: autorange
params.description: automatically calculate the minMidi and maxMidi parameters - 0 by default

pw.name: pw

pwrate.name: pwrate

pwsweep.name: pwsweep
pwsweep.description: Controls the lfo sweep for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

queryArc.description: Query haps inside the given time span.

rand.description: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between 0 and 1.

rand2.name: rand2
rand2.description: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between -1 and 1

randcat.name: randcat

randomSample.returns: number — A random number from -1 to 1.

range.name: range
range.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1.
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range.
Most useful in combination with continuous patterns.

range2.name: range2
range2.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range.

rangex.name: rangex
rangex.description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range,
following an exponential curve.

ratio.name: ratio
ratio.description:
Allows dividing numbers via list notation using ":".
Returns a new pattern with just numbers.

rdim.name: rdim
rdim.description:

reallocateChannelsIfNeeded.name: reallocateChannelsIfNeeded
reallocateChannelsIfNeeded.description:

(channel numbers may lety during lifecycle)

ref.name: ref

register.name: register

replicate.name: replicate
replicate.description:
Experimental

replicate is similar to fast in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count
accordingly. So stepcat("a b".replicate(2), "c d") would be the same as "a b a b c d", whereas
stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d") would be the same as "[a b] [a b] c d".

TODO: find out how this function differs from extend
examples:
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - cp").replicate(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)

reset.name: reset
reset.description: Resets the pattern to the start of the cycle for each onset of the reset pattern.

restart.name: restart
restart.description:
Restarts the pattern for each onset of the restart pattern.
While reset will only reset the current cycle, restart will start from cycle 0.

rev.name: rev
rev.description: Reverse all cycles in a pattern. See also revv for reversing a whole pattern.

revv.name: revv
revv.description: Reverse a whole pattern. See also rev for reversing each cycle.

rfade.name: rfade

samples.description: Loads a collection of samples to use with s

saw2.name: saw2
saw2.description: A sawtooth signal between -1 and 1 (like saw, but bipolar).

scale.name: scale
scale.description:
Turns numbers into notes in the scale (zero indexed) or quantizes notes to a scale.

When describing notes via numbers, note that negative numbers can be used to wrap backwards
in the scale as well as sharps or flats to produce notes outside of the scale.

Also sets scale for other scale operations, like {@link Pattern#scaleTranspose}.

A scale consists of a root note (e.g. c4, c, f#, bb4) followed by semicolon (':') and then a scale type.

The scale name must be written without spaces (because it would be interpreted as a multi-step pattern otherwise).
If your scale name includes spaces, replace them with colons.

The root note defaults to octave 3, if no octave number is given.

scaleTrans.name: scaleTrans
scaleTrans.description:
Transposes notes inside the scale by the number of steps.
Expected to be called on a Pattern which already has a {@link Pattern#scale}

params.name: offset

scaleTranspose.description:

params.name: offset

scope.description: Renders an oscilloscope for the time domain of the audio signal.

params.description: if 1, the scope will be aligned to the first zero crossing. defaults to 1

params.name: color
params.description: line color as hex or color name. defaults to white.

params.name: pos
params.description: y-position relative to screen height. 0 = top, 1 = bottom of screen

params.name: trigger
params.description: amplitude value that is used to align the scope. defaults to 0.

scramble.name: scramble
scramble.description:
Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts at random. Similar to shuffle,
but parts might be played more than once, or not at all, per cycle.

scrub.name: scrub
scrub.description:
Allows you to scrub an audio file like a tape loop by passing values that represents the position in the audio file
in the optional array syntax ex: "0.5:2", the second value controls the speed of playback

seed.name: seed
seed.description:
Change the seed for random signals. Normally, random signals depend on time,
so two patterns at the same time will have the same random values. Specifying
a new seed changes the signal output by rand. This also affects other functions
that use randomness, like shuffle and sometimes.

params.name: n
params.description: A new seed. Can be any number.

examples:
$: s("hh*4").degrade();
$: s("bd*4").degrade().seed(1); // Will degrade different events from the hi-hat

seg.name: seg
seg.description: Samples the pattern at a rate of n events per cycle. Useful for turning a continuous pattern into a discrete one.

segment.name: segment
segment.description: Samples the pattern at a rate of n events per cycle. Useful for turning a continuous pattern into a discrete one.

seq.name: seq
seq.description: Like cat, but the items are crammed into one cycle.

seqPLoop.name: seqPLoop
seqPLoop.description:
Similarly to arrange, allows you to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles.
Unlike arrange, you specify a start and stop time for each pattern rather than duration, which
means that patterns can overlap.

sequence.name: sequence
sequence.description: Like cat, but the items are crammed into one cycle.

sequenceP.name: sequenceP
sequenceP.description: Takes a list of patterns, and returns a pattern of lists.

setContext.name: setContext
setContext.description: Returns a new pattern with the context field set to every hap set to the given value.

setcpm.name: setcpm
setcpm.description: Changes the global tempo to the given cycles per minute

setGainCurve.name: setGainCurve
setGainCurve.description:
Apply a function to all gains provided in patterns. Can be used to rescale gain to be
quadratic, exponential, etc. rather than linear

params.name: function
params.description: to apply to all gain values

examples:
setGainCurve((x) => x * x) // quadratic gain
s("bd*4").gain(0.5) // equivalent to 0.25 gain normally

setMaxPolyphony.name: setMaxPolyphony
setMaxPolyphony.description:
Set the max polyphony. If notes are ringing out via release then they will
start to die out in first-in-first-out order once the max polyphony has been hit

shape.name: shape
shape.description:
(Deprecated) Wave shaping distortion. WARNING: can suddenly get unpredictably loud.
Please use distort instead, which has a more predictable response curve
second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output

shiftInputBuffers.name: shiftInputBuffers
shiftInputBuffers.description: Shift left content of input buffers to receive new web audio block

shiftOutputBuffers.name: shiftOutputBuffers
shiftOutputBuffers.description: Shift left content of output buffers to receive new web audio block

shiftPeaks.name: shiftPeaks
shiftPeaks.description: Shift peaks and regions of influence by pitchFactor into new specturm

showFirstCycle.name: showFirstCycle
showFirstCycle.description: More human-readable version of the firstCycleValues accessor.

shrink.name: shrink
shrink.description:
Experimental

Progressively shrinks the pattern by 'n' steps until there's nothing left, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with :),
that number of times.
A positive number will progressively drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

shuffle.name: shuffle
shuffle.description:
Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts in random order.
Each part will be played exactly once per cycle.

sine2.name: sine2
sine2.description: A sine signal between -1 and 1 (like sine, but bipolar).

size.name: size
size.description:
Sets the room size of the reverb, see room.
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

slice.name: slice
slice.description:
Chops samples into the given number of slices, triggering those slices with a given pattern of slice numbers.
Instead of a number, it also accepts a list of numbers from 0 to 1 to slice at specific points.

slider.name: slider
slider.description: Displays a slider widget to allow the user manipulate a value

slow.name: slow
slow.description: Slow down a pattern over the given number of cycles. Like the "/" operator in mini notation.

slowcat.name: slowcat
slowcat.description: The given items are concatenated, where each one takes one cycle.

slowcatPrime.name: slowcatPrime
slowcatPrime.description: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle. Unlike slowcat, this version will skip cycles.

slowchunk.name: slowchunk
slowchunk.description: Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

slowChunk.name: slowChunk
slowChunk.description: Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

someCyclesBy.name: someCyclesBy
someCyclesBy.description:
Randomly applies the given function by the given probability on a cycle by cycle basis.
Similar to sometimesBy

sometimes.name: sometimes
sometimes.description: Applies the given function with a 50% chance

sometimesBy.name: sometimesBy
sometimesBy.description:
Randomly applies the given function by the given probability.
Similar to someCyclesBy

sortHapsByPart.name: sortHapsByPart
sortHapsByPart.description:
Returns a new pattern, which returns haps sorted in temporal order. Mainly
of use when comparing two patterns for equality, in tests.

separated by ':'.

soundAlias.description: Register an alias for a sound.

params.description: The alias to use for the sound

examples: s("bd hh sd hh").slow(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]/2")

spectrum.name: spectrum
spectrum.description: Renders a spectrum analyzer for the incoming audio signal.

speed.name: speed
speed.description: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

params.name: speed
params.description: inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

params.description: Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:

params.name: stretch
params.description: controls the rotations per cycle ratio, where 1 = 1 cycle / 360 degrees

params.name: cap
params.description: style of line ends: butt (default), round, square

params.description: number of rotations before spiral starts (default 3)

params.name: playheadColor
params.description: color of playhead, defaults to white

params.name: playheadLength

params.name: playheadThickness
params.description: thickness of playheadrotations, defaults to thickness

params.description: steadyness of spiral vs playhead. 1 = spiral doesn't move, playhead does.

splice.name: splice
splice.description: Works the same as slice, but changes the playback speed of each slice to match the duration of its step.

splitQueries.name: splitQueries
splitQueries.description:
Returns a new pattern, with queries split at cycle boundaries. This makes
some calculations easier to express, as all haps are then constrained to
happen within a cycle.

spread.name: spread
spread.description: Set the stereo pan spread for supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").spread("<0 .3 1>")

square2.name: square2
square2.description: A square signal between -1 and 1 (like square, but bipolar).

squeeze.name: squeeze
squeeze.description:
Pick from the list of values (or patterns of values) via the index using the given
pattern of integers. The selected pattern will be compressed to fit the duration of the selecting event
examples: note(squeeze("<0@2 [1!2] 2>", ["g a", "f g f g" , "g a c d"]))

squiz.name: squiz
squiz.description:
Made by Calum Gunn. Reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter. The SuperCollider manual defines Squiz as:

"A simplistic pitch-raising algorithm. It's not meant to sound natural; its sound is reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter, depending on the input. The algorithm works by cutting the signal into fragments (delimited by upwards-going zero-crossings) and squeezing those fragments in the time domain (i.e. simply playing them back faster than they came in), leaving silences inbetween. All the parameters apart from memlen can be modulated."

params.name: squiz
params.description: Try passing multiples of 2 to it - 2, 4, 8 etc.

src.name: src
src.description: Define a custom webaudio node to use as a sound source.

stack.name: stack
stack.description: The given items are played at the same time at the same length.

stepalt.name: stepalt
stepalt.description:
Experimental

Concatenates patterns stepwise, according to an inferred 'steps per cycle'.
Similar to stepcat, but if an argument is a list, the whole pattern will alternate between the elements in the list.
examples:
stepalt(["bd cp", "mt"], "bd").sound()
// The same as "bd cp bd mt bd".sound()

stepcat.name: stepcat

'Concatenates' patterns like fastcat, but proportional to a number of steps per cycle.
The steps can either be inferred from the pattern, or provided as a [length, pattern] pair.
Has the alias timecat.
examples:
stepcat("bd sd cp","hh hh").sound()
// the same as "bd sd cp hh hh".sound()

strans.name: strans
strans.description:
Transposes notes inside the scale by the number of steps.

stripContext.description: Returns a new pattern with the context field of every hap set to an empty object.

struct.description: Applies the given structure to the pattern:
examples:
note("c,eb,g")
  .struct("x ~ x ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~")
  .slow(2)

stutWith.description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

sus.name: sus

sustain.name: sustain
sustain.description: Amplitude envelope sustain level: The level which is reached after attack / decay, being sustained until the offset.

swingBy.name: swingBy
swingBy.description: The function swingBy x n breaks each cycle into n slices, and then delays events in the second half of each slice by the amount x, which is relative to the size of the (half) slice. So if x is 0 it does nothing, 0.5 delays for half the note duration, and 1 will wrap around to doing nothing again. The end result is a shuffle or swing-like rhythm

take.name: take
take.description:
Experimental

Takes the given number of steps from a pattern (dropping the rest).
A positive number will take steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.
examples:
"bd cp ht mt".take("2").sound()
// The same as "bd cp".sound()

"bd cp ht mt".take("1 2 3").sound()
// The same as "bd bd cp bd cp ht".sound()

"bd cp ht mt".take("-1 -2 -3").sound()
// The same as "mt ht mt cp ht mt".sound()

tour.name: tour
tour.description:
Experimental

Inserts a pattern into a list of patterns. On the first repetition it will be inserted at the end of the list, then moved backwards through the list
on successive repetitions. The patterns are added together stepwise, with all repetitions taking place over a single cycle. Using pace to set the
number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
examples:
"[c g]".tour("e f", "e f g", "g f e c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)

trans.name: trans
trans.description:
Change the pitch of each value by the given amount. Expects numbers or note strings as values.
The amount can be given as a number of semitones or as a string in interval short notation.
If you don't care about enharmonic correctness, just use numbers. Otherwise, pass the interval of
the form: ST where S is the degree number and T the type of interval with


M = major

m = minor

P = perfect

A = augmented

d = diminished


Examples intervals:


1P = unison

3M = major third

3m = minor third

4P = perfect fourth

4A = augmented fourth

5P = perfect fifth

5d = diminished fifth

params.name: amount
params.description: Either number of semitones or interval string.

voicing.name: voicing
voicing.description:
Turns chord symbols into voicings. You can use the following control params:


chord: Note, followed by chord symbol, e.g. C Am G7 Bb^7

dict: voicing dictionary to use, falls back to default dictionary

anchor: the note that is used to align the chord

mode: how the voicing is aligned to the anchor

below: top note <= anchor

duck: top note <= anchor, anchor excluded

above: bottom note >= anchor




offset: whole number that shifts the voicing up or down to the next voicing

n: if set, the voicing is played like a scale. Overshooting numbers will be octaved


All of the above controls are optional, except chord.
If you pass a pattern of strings to voicing, they will be interpreted as chords.
